readme:
# Python Environments

Finds, creates and switches Python environments — venv, uv, conda, pyenv, poetry, pipenv and the system interpreter — and activates the selected one in your terminals.

This is the unmodified extension published on Open VSX, pinned to a specific version and verified to work in Diode. It ships platform-specific builds with the native environment locator inside; the registry entry carries one artifact per platform.

## What works in Diode

The extension finds the environments of your workspace and picks one per project; the status bar shows it. With `"python-envs.terminal.autoActivationType": "shellStartup"` in settings.json, every new terminal opens with that environment already active, without a visible `source …/activate` and without edits to your shell profile.

Set `"python.useEnvironmentsExtension": true` to get the **Python** sidebar (View: Show Python) with the Python Projects and Environment Managers views.

## What does not

The default activation mode, `"command"`, types `source …/activate` into a new terminal once shell integration is up. In Diode that step never runs yet, so terminals open without the environment: switch to `"shellStartup"`. Without `"python.useEnvironmentsExtension": true` the Python sidebar stays hidden: VS Code enables it through an experiment, and Diode has none.
